newsitem.title: UK: US stocks in London on standby ahead of jobs data.
newsitem.headline: US stocks in London on standby ahead of jobs data.

text.p: U.S. shares were little changed in quiet European trade on Friday as investors awaited the key U.S. unemployment data, due at 1330 GMT.
The ghost of the February 1996 non-farm total of 705,000, which resulted in the biggest one-day fall of U.S. Treasuries last year, haunted dealing rooms across the globe, strategists said.
"The market is extremely bearish going into this number," said David Coleman, economist at the Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce.
"The view is building that were going to get a hike this month. A strong number either on the non-farms or the wage component will hit the market's nerves ahead of the (U.S. FOMC March 25) meeting."
The non-farm total is forecast to rise by 230,000 in February, down from 271,000 in January, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
The average hourly wage component is expected to increase by 0.4 percent from 0.1 percent a month ago.

A jump in either figure would raise fears that the Fed, keen to keep U.S. economic growth and inflation under control, would use its next monetary policy meeting in 18 days time, to push up its short-term funds rate.
"It's anyone's guess how the market will react to a big number. It's weathered the storm before," one market maker said.
"But I get the feeling that the market is looking for a reason to sell. We've had such a good run that a bit of profit-taking could be a good thing."

Boeing was down $1/2 at $103-7/8 after United Airlines said it had ordered an additional number of aircraft from European manufacturer Airbus and cut an existing order previously placed with the U.S. aircraft maker.
Elsewhere, Eli Lilly, which dropped $2-1/2 to $86-5/8 in New York on Thursday, was up $3/8 to $87 after the company issued a statement concerning one of its products.

In reply to a report issued last week by two Wall Street drug industry analysts, Eli Lilly on Thursday said it was unaware of physicians having problems switching schizophrenia patients from older treatments to Lilly's new antipsychotic drug, Zyprexa.
The March T-bond was down 4/32 to 109-29/32 while the yield on the 30-year cash long bond was standing at 6.89 percent by 1125 GMT.
The March S&P 500 futures contract was down 0.55 to 800.05.
